envelope_digest_caveat: envelope_digest is computed over round(peak, 9), so a matching digest is necessary but NOT sufficient for bit-exact envelope equality. This freeze additionally compares the production-resolved envelope bit-exactly against COMMON_RESOURCE_ENVELOPE.json and against the envelope all 21 calibration runs actually used.

known_output_gaps.status: NOT RECORDABLE without changing frozen code
known_output_gaps.why: certify() computes delivered_obj internally (exp4_certify.py:258) but CertifiedResult has no field for it and payload() does not emit it. Exposing it means editing src/cota_opt, which breaks the frozen-source guard; recomputing it means a duplicate gen1 solve per candidate, roughly 11-17h across 200.
known_output_gaps.recorded_instead: objective_APPROXIMATE (the discovery score, a DIFFERENT quantity) and round_trajectory[1], the objective after round 1, which is an exact upper bound on the delivered objective.

known_output_gaps.status: NOT RECORDABLE without changing frozen code
known_output_gaps.why: certify() extracts only the system max (fitness.peak_vehicles) from FitnessVector; per-period peak_by_period is not carried into the payload. Rebuilding the model in the launcher to recompute it would duplicate the expensive path-set setup.
known_output_gaps.recorded_instead: fitness_EXACT.peak_vehicles (system max), the per-period peak_caps envelope, and the fact that BOTH feasibility arms are enforced in-loop by frequency._feasible:374 so no returned plan can violate either. hours feasibility is additionally re-verified independently in the launcher.

exact_peak_envelope_used_by_this_run.note: Lossless record of the EXACT peak-vehicle envelope this production run used, preserved per Ian's instruction of 23 Sep. Added AFTER the run started; purely additive, alters no existing field, and does not change what the run is doing.

envelope_digest_insufficiency.finding: envelope_digest is NOT sufficient to establish bit-exact peak-envelope identity.
envelope_digest_insufficiency.mechanism: scripts/exp4n_freeze_envelope.py:100-105 computes the digest over round(peak[p], 9) and round(VH_CAP, 9). Two envelopes differing below the 9th decimal place therefore produce the SAME digest.
envelope_digest_insufficiency.how_it_surfaced: The first draft of the production contract freeze compared the peak envelope against constants transcribed by hand from a rounded log line. midday and evening were wrong in the last ULP (159.17277777777778 vs the true 159.17277777777775; 140.19458333333333 vs 140.19458333333336). The digest matched in both cases and would not have caught the discrepancy. The explicit bit-exact assertion did.
envelope_digest_insufficiency.why_this_run_is_still_protected: This run's envelope identity does not rest on the digest. scripts/exp4n_freeze_production_contract.py asserts the production-resolved envelope bit-exactly against COMMON_RESOURCE_ENVELOPE.json AND bit-exactly against the envelope all 21 calibration results actually recorded. Both passed. The digest is corroborating evidence, not the proof.

deferred_action.when: AFTER EXP4N completes. Explicitly NOT retrofitted into this contract.
deferred_action.what: Add a separate exact-envelope fingerprint for future experiments: a hash over a canonical lossless representation of the envelope - raw IEEE-754 bit patterns, or float.hex(), rather than a rounded decimal.
deferred_action.constraint: Must NOT be used to invalidate this run, and must NOT replace envelope_digest in artifacts this run already wrote. It is an ADDITIONAL fingerprint for experiments that come after.
deferred_action.material_already_present: exact_peak_envelope_used_by_this_run above carries the raw bit patterns, so the future fingerprint can be computed over this run's envelope retroactively for comparison, without re-resolving anything.
